## Slide 1: One person, several provider logins

Let me make this concrete with Maya. Maya is a made-up example of someone who works in a clinic. She needs to use several providers’ portals, and each one has its own account.

On the left, you can see the awkward part: before Maya can get into a portal, she has to work out which login belongs to that provider. The account is separate even though, from her point of view, she’s still just Maya doing her job.

On the right is the idea we’re proposing: one account that she can use across providers. That would give her fewer logins to remember and choose between.

We haven’t measured time savings or gathered customer survey results, so I’m not putting a number on the benefit. The point is simply to make access less awkward. I’m happy to talk through it.

speech.md.content:
## Slide 1: One person, several provider logins

Let me make this concrete with Maya. Maya is a made-up example of someone who works in a clinic. She needs to use several providers’ portals, and each one has its own account.

On the left, you can see the awkward part: before Maya can get into a portal, she has to work out which login belongs to that provider. The account is separate even though, from her point of view, she’s still just Maya doing her job.

On the right is the idea we’re proposing: one account that she can use across providers. That would give her fewer logins to remember and choose between.

We haven’t measured time savings or gathered customer survey results, so I’m not putting a number on the benefit. The point is simply to make access less awkward. I’m happy to talk through it.
